To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) active learning strategies, including competency preconditioning, are more effective than traditional lecture-based curricula, (b) active learning strategies improve medical students' performance and physician attributes, and (c) competency assessments are enhanced with active learning strategies.
• Active learning and competency preconditioning are effective in strengthening osteopathic medical student performance, physician attributes and competency assessments.

1) the use of active learning strategies in the preclinical years of medical education improves student performance and physician attributes; 2) active learning improves student performance in the form of higher grades and higher scores on national board exams; and 3) active learning improves physician attributes such as communication, professionalism, and teamwork, and also improves students' self-assessed competence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new learning strategy that is based on the integration of active learning and competency preconditioning, and the evaluation of its effectiveness.
the impact of active learning on osteopathic medical student performance, physician attributes, and competency assessment.
